harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured and verified a healthy three-member MariaDB Galera cluster. All members accept replicated writes, retain availability with one member stopped, and automatically resynchronize it after restart.
actions_performed: Installed MariaDB 10.11.14, Galera 4, rsync, and supporting packages on node1, node2, and node3.
Configured unique node addresses, a shared three-member gcomm address, ROW/InnoDB settings, rsync state transfer, and a recoverable 256 MiB gcache.
Bootstrapped node1 exactly once and joined node2 and node3 normally.
Proved writes and reads through every member, including TCP connections to each $NODE_IP.
Stopped only node3, verified node1 and node2 remained writable at cluster size 2, then restarted node3 normally and observed automatic state transfer and IST.
Removed all temporary TCP probe users and credential files. Final services are active and enabled on every node.

evidence.summary: Formation progressed from size 1 to 2 to 3. Final checks show all three unique node addresses, the same cluster UUID and membership list, Primary/Connected/Ready/Synced state, active/enabled services, and SQL/Galera listeners.

evidence.requirement: Writes through any member are available from the others
evidence.summary: Each managed-node IP accepted a distinct TCP write (rows 401–403). Every member subsequently returned all three rows and identical totals while Synced at cluster size 3.

evidence.requirement: Availability with one member unavailable and automatic resynchronization on return
evidence.summary: Healthy baseline was size 3. node3 was then inactive with its listeners absent; node1 and node2 stayed Primary/Ready at size 2 and exchanged writes 201/202. A normal node3 service start triggered automatic state transfer and IST through seqno 12, restored Synced size 3, recovered both outage-period rows, and allowed node3 to write row 303 back to every member.

attempts.error: The Antrieb managed cluster lease expired at 2026-09-01T16:19:52.349000+00:00

diagnosis.summary: Attempt 1 is unscorable for MariaDB/Galera correctness and should be classified as an environment/lease failure, not a configuration failure. The lease expired before any audited command reached a node, so there is no evidence that MariaDB was inspected, configured, changed, or tested. The executor’s retry reasonably confirmed that the condition was terminal, but evidence is insufficient to assess any task requirement.

evidence.finding: All four terminal calls returned cluster_expired; the first occurred at 16:35:10Z, about 15 minutes after lease expiration. There were no successful terminal records.
The attempted commands were read-only baseline checks on all three nodes plus one node1 retry; every call was rejected before execution.
The executor reported no configuration changes, no replacement cluster, and no Harbor evidence IDs because commands never reached the nodes.
No evidence exists for three-member membership, cross-node replication, availability after losing one member, or automatic resynchronization after its return.

likely_causes.cause: The benchmark failed because the managed-cluster lease had already expired before node execution began.
A scheduling delay, stale allocation, or insufficient lease window may have caused execution to start after expiration; the supplied evidence does not identify which.
MariaDB, Galera, network, or executor configuration defects caused the failure.

next_attempt_guidance: Start work immediately on the fresh allocation and first confirm all three nodes are reachable; stop and report promptly if the bridge reports a lease problem.

Follow the platform discovery order: primer, relevant runbook search, exact image metadata/reference, then small POSIX-sh diagnostic calls. Do not assume package state, credentials, sudo support, or helper paths.
Record baseline evidence on every node: addresses/routes, MariaDB/Galera versions, service state, listeners, and relevant logs.

Apply one consistent Galera configuration using the three actual node addresses, unique node names/addresses, and the required replication, IST, and SST settings. Confirm required ports are reachable before adding speculative firewall rules.
Bootstrap exactly one new primary component, start the other two as joiners, and verify Primary/Connected/Ready/Synced state and cluster size 3 on every member.
Prove bidirectional behavior by writing distinct test data through each member and reading it from the other two.
Stop only one member. Verify the remaining two retain a Primary component, accept writes, and report cluster size 2.
Restart the stopped member without re-bootstrapping. Verify it automatically performs IST or SST, becomes Synced, returns the cluster to size 3, and receives data written while it was unavailable.
Capture command outputs and stable evidence IDs for every requirement; package installation or service-active status alone is not proof of task completion.
